t: #2271 Maximum White Tiles Covered by a Carpet
o: Place a carpet of fixed length anywhere on the number line to maximize covered white tiles; tiles are disjoint intervals. In example 1 the carpet [10,19] covers 9 tiles. An optimal carpet can always be shifted so its left edge coincides with some tile's left endpoint (or equivalently its right edge with a tile's right endpoint), so it suffices to try each tile start as the carpet start. With n up to 5e4 we need prefix sums plus two pointers or binary search rather than trying every position.
k: WLOG the carpet starts exactly at some tile's left endpoint li.
Prefix sums over tile lengths let us compute full segments covered in O(1).
Two pointers: as the left segment index advances, the furthest fully covered segment index only moves right.

a.n: Approach 1: Sorting + prefix sums + two pointers
a.i: Sort tiles and build prefix sums of tile lengths. For each candidate start tiles[i][0], advance j while the span tiles[j][1] - tiles[i][0] + 1 fits in the carpet; segments i..j-1 are fully covered, and segment j (if any) is partially covered by the remaining carpet length.
s: Sort tiles; build pre[k] = total tiles among first k segments.
For each i, advance j while tiles[j][1] - tiles[i][0] + 1 <= carpetLen.
Coverage = pre[j] - pre[i] plus max(0, tiles[i][0] + carpetLen - tiles[j][0]).
Answer is the maximum coverage over all i.
a.t: O(n log n) — sorting dominates; the two-pointer sweep is O(n).

a.i: Same reduction (carpet starts at tiles[i][0]), but find the last segment fully covered by binary searching the sorted list of right endpoints for the largest tiles[j][1] < start + carpetLen. Useful when the window pointers would not be monotonic (e.g., online queries).
s: Sort tiles; keep arrays of left endpoints and prefix sums.
For each i, binary search the largest j with tiles[j][1] <= tiles[i][0] + carpetLen - 1.
Coverage = pre[j+1] - pre[i] plus partial overlap with segment j+1.

c.python:
from bisect import bisect_right
class Solution:
    def maximumWhiteTiles(self, tiles, carpetLen):
        tiles.sort()
        n = len(tiles)
        pre = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i, (l, r) in enumerate(tiles):
            pre[i + 1] = pre[i] + r - l + 1
        ans = 0
        for i in range(n):
            limit = tiles[i][0] + carpetLen - 1
            j = bisect_right([t[1] for t in tiles], limit)  # segments fully covered: i..j-1
            cov = pre[j] - pre[i]
            if j < n:
                cov += max(0, limit - tiles[j][0] + 1)
            ans = max(ans, cov)
        return ans

a.t: O(n log n) — sorting plus a binary search per start.

w: Prefer the two-pointer version in interviews — it is simpler and faster. Pitfalls: forgetting to sort, 32-bit overflow of coordinates near 1e9, mishandling a single tile longer than the carpet (answer capped at carpetLen), and gaps between tiles (the partial-overlap term must not count gap cells). Follow-up: multiple carpets, or weighted tiles.
